title: Why Mary Mallon was locked on an island
topic: Why Mary Mallon was kept on an island for decades

lines: Mary brandished a kitchen fork like a sword, refusing anyone entry.
Neighbors laughed, calling her a stubborn cook who feared losing work.
They dismissed the doctor's warnings as mere gossip.
Police dragged her to Willard Parker Hospital.
Scientists tested her stool three times each week.
The bacteria hid in her gallbladder, impossible to cure.
You see, it’s like a broken spoon.
It keeps poisoning every bowl of soup.
She kept cooking, spreading typhoid to dozens and causing three deaths.
The city locked her on North Brother Island to stop more outbreaks.
Other carriers were released, given jobs, and paid rent.
She became a scapegoat because she was a woman cook.
When she tried to work again in 1914, another outbreak erupted.
Investigators matched her handwriting and sent her back to the island.
She spent the rest of her life baking cakes for fellow patients.

claims.claim: Mallon was forcibly quarantined on North Brother Island after being identified as a typhoid carrier and remained there until her death in 1938.
Her long confinement was unique; other asymptomatic carriers were not held for decades, reflecting gender and occupational bias.
After a 1915 outbreak at Sloane Maternity Hospital, investigators linked the illness to Mallon and returned her to the island.
